formal_scope: The Möbius function is the actual rational-valued incidence-algebra inverse, not a free weight satisfying an assumed conclusion.
The exact-top indicator and tested finite-set cardinality formula are fully proved.
The exact-top SubMulAction, its actual fixed-point subtype, and the actual orbit quotient satisfy the Möbius/Burnside formula.
Order-automorphic transport proves the required invariance; individual support sublevels need not be invariant.
An equivariant base map gives the actual stabilizer subgroup action on its fiber. A subtype equivalence converts its sublevel count to the ambient base/fixed/support conjunction.
Each stabilizer-fiber count and their sum over any finite representative set are proved. Empty exact-support subsets and fibers are allowed.

The actual ambient orbit quotient is equivalent to the disjoint union of actual stabilizer-fiber orbit quotients under precisely stated representative coverage and separation. This part requires no finiteness.
Commuting the exact-support restriction with the base-fiber restriction is an actual equivariant subtype equivalence, transferred to quotient sets.

The global orbit cardinal equals the full sum of Mobius/Burnside fiber counts. Classical quotient representatives are selected in Lean, with their coverage and separation proved; unused base orbits contribute empty fibers.
The final order_automorphic_admissible_extension_orbit_count constructs exact-support invariance from the paper equivariance hypothesis; it does not assume a counting or bijection conclusion.
not_formalized: Source-specific admissibility tests, geometric recognition, generation, stabilizer computations and census completeness.
Divisor-poset identification with the number-theoretic Möbius function, least-field support facts and Frobenius freeness.
A complete new formalization of the whole Topic D manuscript.
hypotheses: Finite group and finite acted-on set for orbit averaging; arbitrary finite tested set for exact-top count.

Finite partial order with greatest element, decidable equality/order and a locally finite interval structure. The latter is available for every finite poset via Fintype.toLocallyFiniteOrder; it is not an extra mathematical restriction.

Exact-top invariance, derived by top_support_invariant from equivariance under a family of order isomorphisms. No group-action axioms on that family are needed beyond those on the object action and the stated equivariance.
Equivariance of the base map for the actual extension-fiber adapter.

For arbitrary indexed transversals: every object base can be translated to a representative, and two representatives in the same base orbit have the same index. These are separately discharged for canonical quotient representatives.
The manuscript invariant admissibility subset R is the acted-on type X in this formal interface; constructing a particular source-specific R remains the application responsibility.
